summary.headline: Menon Bearings Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 36.57% to INR91.79 crores and PAT 67.35%, with management reiterating INR360 crore FY27 revenue as conservative.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly sales, EBITDA, PBT and PAT for Q1 FY27, with consolidated sales of INR91.79 crores (up 36.57%) and PBT of INR18.51 crores (up 67.36%). Standalone bi-metal sales rose to INR67.06 crores (up ~40%). Growth was attributed to export and new customer wins following a June 2026 US and Canada marketing trip, plus a shift in product mix toward brakes, where EBITDA margin reached about 25%. Management said the FY27 revenue guidance of INR360 crores is conservative, and described a domestic RFQ pipeline of over INR75 crores. Several new-business timelines (Alkop US customers, railway brake approval) run into FY28 and beyond.

segments.name: Bi-metal (Menon Bearings)
segments.commentary: Q1 standalone sales INR67.06 crores; EBITDA margin around 21%+ per management. Utilisation about 80% on machinery basis; Rs 9-10 crore capex this year expected to add 25-30% capacity.

segments.name: Aluminium (Menon Alkop)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin around 21%. Utilisation 65-70%. Management targets Alkop revenue of INR100 crores this year and INR125 crores next year; quarterly run rate cited by an analyst at about INR21 crores.

segments.name: Brakes (Menon Brakes)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin about 25% in Q1, up from about 12-14% previously, attributed mainly to product mix and lower Dubai/Africa export volumes. Utilisation 65-70%. Railway dynamometer expected by end-August 2026, with testing rig running by September-end.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR360 crores, which management called conservative; mid-20% growth possible, with internal target of INR500 crores reached sooner than 2030.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to sustain around 20-21% over time; management said brake margin of 25% may fall next quarter.
Additional business of INR65-75 crores for current and next FY, subject to good monsoon and no worsening geopolitics.
Domestic RFQ list above INR75 crores; at 75-80% conversion, management expects more than INR60 crores of additional business within this year and next.
Export share of revenue expected to rise to about 37% next year; FY27 export share was described as around 24-30% historically.
capex_capacity: Bi-metal: Rs 9-10 crores capex this FY to add roughly 25-30% capacity; expected to yield revenue above INR25 crores. Peak bi-metal revenue on current capacity cited above INR400 crores.
Alkop: about INR4 crores capex this year; 65,000 sq ft new building with 25,000-30,000 sq ft still available for machines already ordered.

Brakes: dynamometer under construction, expected by end-August 2026; railway approval, then testing for about one year. Railway business INR5-6 crores in year one, scaling to INR25-30 crores within two years.

Management says current infrastructure supports up to about INR500 crores revenue; about seven acres of empty land at the aluminium plant. New land for bi-metal being evaluated for the next two years.
Future capex asset turn about 2.5x; capex to be funded through internal accruals, no fresh loans for bi-metal and Alkop.
demand_pricing: Alkop: RFQs, NDAs and vendor profiling from Magna, Allison Transmission, Linamar-type US customers after June 2026 US and Canada trip; management cites INR50-60 crores potential, realisation expected in 9-12 months (targeting 6-7 months). Samples by 2027.
Bi-metal engine bearing: began receiving RFQs and orders from US customers; supply expected from Q3-Q4 FY27.

Africa: bearings, bushes, washers estimated at about INR9 crores; brake linings INR6-7 crores; existing Dubai distributor business INR7-8 crores per year. Merchant export orders were stalled for three months due to Strait of Hormuz disruption; new orders require 100% advance for the initial six months.
Aluminium realisation above INR900 per unit now, up from about INR700 when aluminium was about INR250-300/kg; aluminium rates now INR340-370.
Competition: China pressure in Dubai and Africa for brake linings; company keeps minimum margins on these exports.
EV share in Alkop about 4-5% now, targeting about 8% within two years; Tata EV parts moved to a 1,600-ton press.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue expected from brakes in FY27 and railway timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Dynamometer by end-August; RDSO vendor code registered; railway audit then approval; INR5-6 crores in year one, INR25-30 crores within two years. Management declined to give precise OEM numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Africa revenue potential and payment terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Bearings, bushes, washers about INR9 crores; brake linings INR6-7 crores; Dubai distributor INR7-8 crores a year. Aluminium excluded; new merchant exporters require 100% advance for initial six months.

qa_highlights.question: Alkop business visibility and FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets INR100 crores this year and INR125 crores next year. US RFQs and NDAs received; new business takes 9-12 months to realise. Europe visit planned for September.

qa_highlights.question: Bi-metal capacity beyond current utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation about 85-87% by one measure, about 80% by management's machinery-based count. Capex of INR9-10 crores adds 25-30% capacity; third shift available.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 INR360 crore guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called INR360 crores conservative, declined to raise the number, and said Q4 would be better.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of margins with raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated margin 20-21% expected over time; brake margin of 25% driven by product mix and may fall next quarter.

risks_watch: Brake margin of 25% is product-mix driven and may fall; management expects consolidated margins of 20-21%.
Monsoon and geopolitical conditions (Strait of Hormuz, war) cited as conditions for the INR65-75 crore additional business.
Railway brake approval timeline is uncertain: testing could run about one year after registration, and orders are unknown.
Raw-material and consumables cost volatility: aluminium up sharply; carbide tools up about 300% per management.
Dependence on export: about 60% of order book is export; US concentration; tariff impact noted earlier.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and pipeline, with repeated optimism about FY27 and beyond. Evasive on hard numbers for brakes, Alkop realisation timing and exact guidance changes, which were left as "conservative" without a revised figure.
key_quotes: we have recorded highest-ever sales, highest -ever EBITDA, highest -ever profit before tax and PAT in the history of the company for this quarter.

The total potential of additional business for the current and next financial year is expected to be around INR65 crores to INR75 crores, subject to good monsoon and geopolitical situation doesn't worsen further.
we are 100% sure that we will get additional business from them and maybe there will be substantial and significant increase in the volumes of Menon Brakes in the next year.
So, INR360 crores, I would say is a conservative figure and we will stick to that.

adds.what: Bi-metal capacity expansion via Rs 9-10 crore capex this FY (adds ~25-30% capacity)
Alkop: 65,000 sq ft new building with 25,000-30,000 sq ft free for machines already ordered (~INR4 crore capex this year)
Railway brake dynamometer and testing rig (Menon Brakes), dynamometer by end-August 2026, rig by September-end

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR360 crore (~28% implied growth vs prior base, called conservative, mid-20% growth possible), backed by a Rs 9-10 crore bi-metal capacity add (+25-30%), Alkop INR100 crore target with 25-30k sq ft free space, and an INR75 crore+ domestic RFQ pipeline; but no firm order book sized to the full guidance and several new-business timelines run into FY28.
